chapter: Family and early memories of Jelly
title: Seeing Jelly at about six; his letters from the West Coast
summary: A memory of Jelly putting a napkin round her neck, and of his travels to Tacoma and the coast.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, then you saw your brother when he was about six. He came over from Biloxi, you say?

I don't know whether he came over here or I went over there. Over there. But I remember—I can remember sitting at the table and him putting a napkin around my neck, so I wouldn't sell my dress, because it was a blue dress that he had bought for me. He bought— And listen, I was so proud of my clothes when he sent me something. I knew I wasn't going to—I didn't have a sense enough to say then I wouldn't meet myself on the street, but I knew now that they were exclusive. Yeah. And I knew of Tacoma, Washington, and let's see, I can't think of the name of the place. Some place he used to write us all the time. Looked like he'd leave Washington and go back there.
He was out on the coast a long time. Yes, he was.

And so many people that knows us, and we never, never mention Jellie, you know, and they'd say, I want you to go down to Cabildo and see this artist down here. He's simply—I said, well, that's my brother. He's on number 30 on the list, you know what I mean? And so Frank said, why wouldn't you speak about him? I said, well, sometimes it hurts.
